bio: Adam Dalton is a color guard instructor, visual designer, and music educator. He marched with The Cavaliers (2002-2004) and was a charter member of The Study Winter Guard. He has served as a color guard instructor for Phantom Regiment, weapon designer for Southwind, and visual designer/choreographer for the Troopers. He holds a Bachelor's in Music Education from James Madison University and founded Creativa Designs, a design and consultation company for marching arts.

Austin Greene is a professional visual designer, music educator, and marching arts adjudicator from Raleigh, NC. He has served on the instructional staff of the Bluecoats, as Visual Caption Head for The Cadets Drum & Bugle Corps, and as Assistant Caption Head for The Cavaliers. He regularly adjudicates for Bands of America, Winter Guard International, and Drum Corps International. He holds a B.S.Ed. in Music Education from Western Carolina University (2003) and a Master of Music in Conducting from the University of Connecticut (2006).

Bret Cappelluti is the Director of Bands at Madera High School in California and holds a BA in Music Performance from San Jose State University and a Masters in Teaching from George Fox University. He performed with the Santa Clara Vanguard, the California Dons, and the Valley Fever Drum and Bugle Corps, and has served as an adjudicator for Drum Corps International, WGI, the Western Band Association, and other organizations.

Brandt Crocker has been the primary DCI announcer — known as "The Voice of DCI" — since the organization's inception in 1972, and has announced every DCI World Championship except four. He began in the marching arts as director of the Americare Stepperettes drill team in 1966, later becoming Business Manager of the Troopers Drum and Bugle Corps in 1969. Beyond DCI, he announces for WGI, high school marching band contests, Marching Mizzou, and the Missouri State University Ozarko Contest, and has served as a contest coordinator, contest promoter, and founder of the Tour Event Partner College.

Brittany Dacy is the Director of Bands at Westwood High School in Austin, Texas, where she directs the marching band, Wind Ensemble, and Symphony Orchestra. She is becoming increasingly active as an adjudicator and clinician for marching and concert bands across America. She holds a Bachelor's in Music Education from UT Austin and a Master's in Band Conducting from Sam Houston State University.

Cecil Adderley has served as an adjudicator for Drum Corps International (DCI). He is Chair of the Music Education Department at Berklee College of Music and holds a Ph.D. in Music Education from the University of South Carolina.

Dr. Cameron "Chip" Crotts is an active adjudicator for Drum Corps International, Bands of America, Winter Guard International, Drum Corps Japan, Taiwan Marching Academy, and Music for All. He currently serves as Brass Caption Head for the 21-time DCI World Champion Blue Devils and has won world championships with multiple drum corps, including Phantom Regiment and Blue Devils. With over 25 years in the drum corps activity, he has also taught on the staffs of Santa Clara Vanguard, The Cavaliers, and Spirit of Atlanta.

Carl Diefenbach has been judging marching bands and drum and bugle corps for 20 years, including DCI, DCA, and competitions across the United States. He is also a clinician, designer, and has served as program advisor for Capital Regiment, with decades of experience spanning military bands, drum corps, and high school to college performing arts.

Craig Dunn is a member of the Drum Corps International judging team and founder/executive director of Rhythm X Indoor Percussion Ensemble. He has taught percussion in central Ohio since 1993, serving as director of percussion at Westerville South High School and Fairborn High School. Dunn served three terms on the WGI Percussion Advisory Board and led Westerville South to multiple WGI regional championships and bronze medals at the WGI World Championships.

Clarke Williams was a DCI Hall of Fame visual judge who judged at the inaugural DCI Championship in 1972 and served for more than 40 years. He began marching at age 8 with the St. Ann's Cadets of Fairlawn, New Jersey, and later taught drum corps and high school bands before becoming a judge through the Eastern States Judges Association in the 1960s. Inducted into the DCI Hall of Fame in 1999, he was known as the 'gentleman judge' and last judged at the 2013 Open Class World Championship Finals. He died on April 20, 2024 at age 82 after a battle with Parkinson's disease.

Carl Nelson is a visual judge with over 35 years of experience in the marching arts, serving as an adjudicator for Drum Corps International (DCI), Winter Guard International (WGI), and Bands of America (BOA). He served as the Visual Proficiency judge for the 2022 DCI World Championship Finals and has also judged at BOA Regional and Grand National Championships, WGI Winds Championships, and DCI Open Class Championships. Nelson resides in Corona, California.

Douglas Henderson marched with the Madison Scouts Drum & Bugle Corps (1998-1999) and taught on the brass staff of the Madison Drum & Bugle Corps Association in 2001. He is active as an adjudicator, guest conductor, and clinician across the United States. He serves as Associate Director of Bands at the University of Texas at Austin, conducting the Wind Symphony and teaching conducting and band literature.

Don (Donald) MacTaggart served as a Drum Corps International adjudicator, judging General Effect Music at the 2008 DCI World Championships Open Class Semifinals and Brass Performance at the 2010 DCI World Championships Open Class Finals.

David Starnes has adjudicated for Drum Corps International, Bands of America, and Winter Guard International since 1994. He served as Design Advisor for Carolina Crown Drum and Bugle Corps (2013–2018) during which the corps won the DCI World Championship, and currently serves as Program Coordinator for The Cavaliers Drum and Bugle Corps. He judged General Effect Music at the 2009 DCI World Class Semifinals at Lucas Oil Stadium. Starnes was inducted into the Bands of America Hall of Fame in 2019.

Edwin Beens is a Dutch marching arts adjudicator who has judged for Color Guard Nederland since 1996 and has served as its Chief Judge and Technical Director since 1998, becoming a Winter Guard International judge in 2000 (Design Analysis and General Effect) while also judging for Drum Corps International, the World Music Contest, WAMSB, and Drum Corps Europe. He was inducted into the CGN Hall of Fame in 2011 for his contributions to color guard and indoor percussion. He started as a drummer at age 8, became a drum major and visual designer, performed twice at WGI World Championships with Art Development, and later joined the staff of Dutch drum corps Blue Wave.

Dr. Gary Schallert is Director of Bands and Professor of Music at Western Kentucky University, where he conducts the Wind Ensemble and Symphonic Band. He is an active adjudicator for prestigious marching arts events including Drum Corps International.

Greg Williams is a BOA Adjudicator and former high school band director who was a member of the Spirit of Atlanta Drum and Bugle Corps. He spent 20 years as Director of Bands at North Cobb High School in Kennesaw, Georgia, and continues to judge high school bands.

J. Bierschenk served as a Visual Proficiency judge for Drum Corps International, adjudicating the Visual Proficiency subcaption at the Open Class 'March On!' event in Champlin, Minnesota, on July 19, 2025.

Jill Moyer was a drum major for the Crossmen drum and bugle corps in 1979–1980 and appears in the 1980 Legacy Collection DVD. She later joined the DCI contest staff as a member of the contest personnel.

Dr. Jason Rinehart is an adjudicator for Drum Corps International and the Central States Judges Association with over 20 years in drum corps. He marched with the Sky Ryders and Phantom Regiment, taught with Pioneer, Capital Regiment, the Boston Crusaders, and The Cadets, and served as Brass Caption Head for the Glassmen and Spirit of Atlanta.
